choices.text: The membrane is a solid wall that stops everything from crossing
The membrane lets everything through freely, like an open door
The membrane is selectively permeable: it lets some things through and keeps others out
Only plant cells have a membrane; animal cells are open

questions.explanation: The trap claim is: The cell membrane is a solid wall that blocks everything from entering or leaving. In fact The membrane is selectively permeable: it lets some things through and keeps others out. Food and oxygen cross in, waste crosses out, and harmful particles are refused.
questions.misconception: The cell membrane is a solid wall that blocks everything from entering or leaving.
questions.prompt: Which statement about the cell membrane is correct?

questions.explanation: Chloroplasts trap light energy to make food and are plant-only. The nucleus, membrane and mitochondrion appear in both cell types.
questions.prompt: Which structure is found in a plant cell but not in an animal cell?

questions.answer: Water fills the vacuole, which pushes the cell contents and membrane hard against the cell wall. The cell is turgid and firm, so the plant stands. Without water the vacuole shrinks, the push fades, cells go flaccid and the plant wilts.
questions.explanation: Firmness is water pressure: a full vacuole presses the membrane against the wall (turgid), an emptied one cannot (flaccid).
questions.prompt: Explain why a plant stands up straight when it has plenty of water, and why it wilts without water.

questions.answer: Leaf cell -> leaf tissue -> leaf (organ) -> shoot system -> whole plant. Similar cells form a tissue, tissues form an organ, organs work together in a system.
questions.explanation: Each rung groups the rung below: cells into tissues, tissues into organs, organs into systems.
questions.prompt: Write the organisation ladder in order, starting from a single leaf cell and ending at the whole shoot system.

choices.text: It traps light energy to make food
It is the control centre that holds the instructions running the cell
It stores water and pushes the cell firm

questions.explanation: The nucleus holds the instructions and controls the cell. Trapping light is the chloroplast, releasing energy is the mitochondrion, and the water push is the vacuole.
questions.prompt: What is the job of the nucleus?
